bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI, focusing on systems that learn from data and improve over time.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: trained on labeled data to predict outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: agent learns by interacting with its environment to maximize rewards.
Model Training: feeding data to learn patterns and minimize prediction differences.
Features and Labels: input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: data split for model training and performance evaluation.
Overfitting: model learns training data too well, performs poorly on new data.
Underfitting: model is too simple, fails to capture important data patterns.
Linear Regression: models linear relationship for continuous output prediction.
Logistic Regression: predicts probability of belonging to a particular class (classification).
Decision Trees: non-linear model splitting data into subsets based on feature values.
Random Forest: ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: fraud detection, credit scoring, and algorithmic trading.
Marketing: customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: processing sensor data, making decisions, and navigating safely.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: evaluate model performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy or MSE.
Cross-Validation: technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data by splitting into subsets.
Hyperparameter Tuning: optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance using techniques like grid search.
Data Quality and Quantity: models require large amounts of accurate, consistent data; labeled data collection can be hard.
Interpretability: complex models (deep learning) are difficult to understand, problematic in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair or unethical outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: common issues where models either learn noise or are too simple to capture patterns.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and Explainable AI (XAI).
Growing computational power and datasets will expand ML's role across industries.
Increased integration into daily life, enabling smarter technologies in various sectors.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential for progress.
